references.text: The departure from Egypt took place in the first month, and the arrival at Sinai in the third month shows the timeframe of the journey.
Confirms that the children of Israel left Egypt in the first month.
Israel's journey through the wilderness of Sin on the way to Sinai, in the second month after leaving Egypt.
The Israelites' stay at Rephidim just before arriving at the wilderness of Sinai.
Refers to the distance from Horeb (Sinai) to Kadesh-Barnea and confirms the geographical significance of Sinai.
Moses' first meeting with God at the mountain of God, later identified as Sinai.
God's promise that the people would serve Him on this mountain is fulfilled upon arrival at Sinai.
Stephen's speech refers to the wilderness of Mount Sinai and Moses' calling.
Stephen mentions the assembly in the wilderness at Mount Sinai.
Paul uses Mount Sinai as an allegory for the old covenant.
Chronological and theological connection: 19:1 marks the arrival at the place where the law (referred to in 7:38) was later given.
Narrative framework: 19:1 marks the arrival at the wilderness of Sinai, while 10:12 marks the departure from the same place.
Temporal contrast showing the duration of the stay: 19:1 is the arrival (year 1), while 1:1 is the resumption of leadership (year 2).
Complementary descriptions of the same event: 19:1 gives the time, while 33:15 confirms the geographical route from Rephidim.
Direct narrative connection within the same chapter: 19:1 marks the arrival, while 19:11 prepares for the holy meeting.
